title: The Lion and the Boar
text:
It was a scorching summer day, and every animal was desperate for water. A lion and a boar reached a small spring at exactly the same moment. Neither would let the other drink first. They argued, then charged, and soon they were locked in a savage fight, tearing at each other with claws and tusks.

After a while both were bleeding and exhausted, and they broke apart to catch their breath before going at it again. As they stood panting, they happened to look up. On the rocks and branches around the spring sat a row of vultures, waiting patiently. The birds did not care which one won. They were only waiting to see which would fall first, so they could eat him.

The lion and the boar looked at the vultures and then at each other. They agreed at once to stop. It was better, they said, to be friends than to become food for vultures. Then they drank, side by side.
lesson: Before a dispute with a colleague goes too far, look around at who benefits from the fight. Often it is someone who wants you both weakened.
source: Aesop's Fables, The Lion and the Boar
